C1.title: Quick Access
C1.text: After dealing the pocket cards, do not distribute the white chips.

C2.title: Noise Sensors
C2.text: Flip the 1-star chips for Rounds 1, 2, and 3 to the dark side. These chips cannot change owners once distributed.

C3.title: Motion Detector
C3.text: If any of the Flop cards (in Round 2) is a J, Q, or K, the player with the white 1-star chip discards their pocket cards and draws new ones.

C4.title: Retina Scan
C4.text: Before the final hand is revealed in the Showdown, the others jointly guess one of the hand's pocket cards (2 to A). If incorrect, the heist fails.

C5.title: Hasty Getaway
C5.text: After the Turn (Round 3), do not distribute the orange chips.

C6.title: Ventilation Shaft
C6.text: Flip the highest-value chips for Rounds 1, 2, and 3 to the dark side. These chips cannot change owners once distributed.

C7.title: Laser Tripwires
C7.text: If none of the Flop cards (in Round 2) is a J, Q, or K, the player with the highest-value white chip discards their pocket cards and draws new ones.

C8.title: Blackout
C8.text: At the beginning of each round, discard all the previous chips.

C9.title: Fingerprint Scan
C9.text: Before the final hand is revealed in the Showdown: All others collectively guess the hand's ranking (e.g., "Royal Flush"). If incorrect, the heist fails.

C10.title: Security Cameras
C10.text: Each player receives three pocket cards instead of two.

S1.title: Informant
S1.text: One of you shows one other player one of your pocket cards.

S2.title: Getaway Driver
S2.text: One of you shares with everyone the rank (e.g., "Royal Flush") of your current hand.

S3.title: Investor
S3.text: After dealing pocket cards, each of you shares with everyone how many "face cards" (J, Q, K) you have.

S4.title: Mastermind
S4.text: Choose a card value (2 to A). One of you shares with everyone how many pocket cards they have of this value.

S5.title: Hacker
S5.text: One of you draws one more pocket card from the deck, then discards one of your pocket cards.

S6.title: Coordinator
S6.text: After dealing pocket cards, each of you gives one of your pocket cards to the player on your left.

S7.title: Jack
S7.text: One of you takes this card, replacing one of your pocket cards. This card is a J that does not belong to any suit.

S8.title: Math Whiz
S8.text: After dealing pocket cards, each of you shares with everyone the sum of your card values. J, Q, K have a value of 10. A has a value of 11.

S9.title: Con Artist
S9.text: After dealing the pocket cards, shuffle and redistribute all the pocket cards.

S10.title: Muscle
S10.text: One of you gains the following ability: Your hand beats every other hand of the same rank.

H1.title: Contingency Planner
H1.text: Deal all players an extra pocket card. Before revealing hands, each player discards a card of their choice.

H2.title: Stunt Driver
H2.text: Before dealing community cards in rounds 2-4, the player who previously took the 1 chip looks at the top card of the deck and may choose to discard it.

H3.title: The Fixer v2
H3.text: One player removes one of their pocket cards from the game, permanently. Return it to the box without showing other players. They cannot reveal what card was removed, even in future hands.

H4.title: Gadgeteer v2
H4.text: Once each, players may each pick up a chip from a previous round, which counts as a suit-less card of its value (e.g., a 3 chip becomes a suit-less 3 card). Once you pick up a chip, you cannot put it back down.

H5.title: Oracle
H5.text: One player may attempt to guess the values (not suits) of the cards in another player's hand. The other player shares how many of the guesses were correct.

H6.title: Gambler v2
H6.text: After dealing pocket cards, collectively choose 1: All players discard their highest card face-up, or all players discard their lowest card face-up. Then, all players draw a card.

H7.title: Card Counter
H7.text: Deal all players an extra pocket card. Before distributing white chips, all players discard their lowest card.

H8.title: Arithmetician
H8.text: One player can share the difference between two of their pocket card values. Ace counts as 11, face cards count as 10.

H9.title: Fisherman
H9.text: One player names a card they don't have (value and suit). If any other player has that card, they reveal it to the table.

H10.title: Artist v2
H10.text: Before dealing pocket cards, go to a random Wikipedia article. Once this hand, one player is allowed to use exactly 5 words from that article's first paragraph to describe their hand.

H11.title: Assassin
H11.text: Choose a community card to discard and replace it with a random card.

H12.title: Contortionist v2
H12.text: One player can halve the value of an even-valued non-face card in their pocket. Turn that card sideways to indicate it is halved. If you halve a 2, it becomes an Ace.

H13.title: Magician
H13.text: Choose a rank other than high-card. That rank does not exist for this hand. (Keep in mind: hands of the removed rank may contain lower-ranked hands, such as 3 of a kind containing a pair)

H14.title: Socialist v2
H14.text: Instead of dealing pocket cards, deal 2 cards in between each pair of players. Each player's "pocket" consists of the cards on either side of them, and they can look at all of them (and can use all 4 in their best hand).

H15.title: Impersonator
H15.text: One player can swap a card from their hand with one of the community cards.

H16.title: Hoarder
H16.text: One player may draw an extra card to add to their pocket.

H17.title: Fraudster
H17.text: When each player reveals their hand in the showdown, they can choose one card to count as 1 higher or lower than its value. A can become K or 2, and vice versa.

H18.title: Harmonizer
H18.text: Choose two suits. Cards of one of those suits count as the other suit as well.

H19.title: The Skipper
H19.text: Choose two adjacent values: they both count as the higher of the two values unless you chose A and 2, which counts as 2. Straights are unaffected.

H20.title: Individualist
H20.text: Before distributing yellow and orange chips, reveal a card from the deck. All players discard their cards of the revealed value.

H21.title: The Anchor
H21.text: One player gains the following ability: Their hand loses to every other hand of the same rank.

H22.title: Philanthropist
H22.text: One player distributes all of their pocket cards to the other players as evenly as possible. If other modifiers cause them to gain additional cards, they distribute them as soon as they receive them.

H23.title: Community Organizer
H23.text: Deal all players 2 extra pocket cards. Whenever a community card would be drawn, players with at least 3 cards can add a pocket card to the community instead. Before distributing red chips, all players discard down to 2 pocket cards.

H24.title: Juggler
H24.text: Two players simultaneously choose a card to exchange with one another.

H25.title: Radio Operator
H25.text: Once per game, each player can give a signal of a thumbs-up or a thumbs-down (but nothing in between). You can agree ahead of time on what these two signals mean.

H26.title: Celebrity
H26.text: This card is an extra player for this hand. Deal their pocket cards face-up. Anybody can assign them a chip.

H27.title: Trainer
H27.text: Before the Showdown, the player with the red 1 chip chooses a hand rank other than the rank of their own hand: all hands with that rank are considered tied.

H28.title: Sacrifice
H28.text: One player adds one of their cards to the community cards.

H29.title: Backup v2
H29.text: Once 3 suits are represented in the community cards, or after all community cards have been added, you may collectively decide to discard all pocket cards that don't share a suit with any community card.

H30.title: Decoy
H30.text: Before evaluating the result of the heist, you can choose to abandon this heist without it counting as a failed heist. If so, start the next heist with the same modifier cards (except for this one).

H31.title: Orchestrator v2
H31.text: After adding community cards in rounds 2-4, all players may pass a card to the player on their right. Shuffle up the cards in your hand before passing so that other players can't tell which card you're passing.

H32.title: Courier
H32.text: After dealing pocket cards, one player passes a card to the player on their right. At the start of each subsequent round, after adding community card(s), the player with the most pocket cards must pass a card to the player on their right.

H33.title: Killer
H33.text: In round 4, any player can point at a light-side chip in front of another player and say "Bang" to kill it. Flip that chip to its dark side. After killing a chip, you can show one of your cards to another player.

H34.title: Categorizer
H34.text: Red and Black cards don't form pairs with each other. You can choose to enable this modifier at any time, but once enabled it must stay enabled.

H35.title: Capitalist
H35.text: Before the Showdown, the player with the red 4 chip draws the highest unique community card into their hand (e.g., if there is a pair of Aces in the community cards, they'd take the next highest non-paired value).

H36.title: Slayer v2
H36.text: One player slays another player. The slayed player discards all Ks. The slayed player must choose Qs in the community to discard and replace with the Ks, if there are any Qs.

H37.title: Snitch
H37.text: Reveal 10 cards from the deck so that all players know they aren't in play.

H38.title: Distributor
H38.text: After round 1, deal face-down cards equal to 1 more than the number of players. From lowest to highest chip, players take turns looking at the cards and choosing one to add to their hand. Discard the remaining card face-up.

H39.title: Puzzlemaster
H39.text: Each player can guess two of another player's pocket card values once. If incorrect, the guesser draws another pocket card.

H40.title: Angler
H40.text: One player can ask another player if they have a certain card value: "Got any ___?" If yes, the questioned player gives a card of the matching value to the questioner. Otherwise, they answer "Go Fish" and the questioner draws an additional pocket card.

H42.title: Stargazer
H42.text: If a card is revealed with value equal to the last chip you took (A = 1), you must reveal and swap your highest rank pocket card with that card. If this loops infinitely, you win the heist.

H43.title: Bloodletter
H43.text: Pocket Hearts can be added to the community cards to draw another card. Hearts cannot form Flushes.

H44.title: Benefactor
H44.text: Once per card, pocket Diamonds can be given to another player to draw another card. Diamonds cannot form Flushes.

H45.title: Pocketeer Rocketeer
H45.text: At any time, a player can discard a pocket A or K and replace it with a random card. If you do, you must also choose another pocket card or community card to discard and replace.

H46.title: War
H46.text: Add cards to the community 1 at a time. If the added card isn't higher than the previously-added card, discard it face-up and add a replacement. Exception: Any card can be added directly after A or K. If you run out of cards in the deck, you win the heist.

H47.title: Guillotine
H47.text: All face cards are discarded and replaced as soon as they enter play.

H48.title: Plumber
H48.text: Choose a suit. Discard all cards of that suit and replace them, except for cards involved in a flush (after choosing the suit, players may reveal that they have a flush involving community cards).

H49.title: Blood on the Clocktower v2
H49.text: Each round, add 1 extra community card when community cards are added. Then, all players vote on a community card to discard by pointing at it simultaneously.

H50.title: Unreliable Intel
H50.text: The lowest Spade in play is a wildcard.

H51.title: Auto-Locks
H51.text: The first player to take a chip in the first three rounds cannot take the highest or lowest chip. Whatever they take, flip it to the dark side.

H52.title: Facial Detection
H52.text: Make your best hand as normal. If you are the only person with your hand rank, your hand beats all players with non-unique ranks.

H53.title: Weight Sensors
H53.text: Before the Showdown, all players reveal their hands. Discard all cards of the highest overall value in anyone's pocket.

H54.title: Omaha Protocol
H54.text: Deal each player two extra pocket cards. Each player must use exactly 2 cards from their hand and 3 cards from the community to make their best hand

H55.title: Nile Protocol
H55.text: In round 4, flip two River cards instead of 1.

H56.title: One-Way Doors v2
H56.text: In Rounds 1-3, flip all chips to their dark side and take them one at a time by following this procedure: Select a random chip that hasn't been distributed yet. Start a 10 second timer. Somebody must take the chip before the timer goes off, or you lose the heist.

H57.title: Double Vault
H57.text: Round 3 must have the chips in the correct order (for the state of the game in Round 3). If not, you lose the heist.

H58.title: 7 Card Stud Protocol
H58.text: This round, there are no community cards. Instead, deal the following cards to each player: Round 1: 2 face-down, 1 face-up. Round 2: 1 face-up. Round 3: 1 face-down. Round 4: 1 face-down, 1 face-up.

H59.title: Signal Jammer
H59.text: Each player's pocket also includes the highest pocket card(s) of the player to their left (but you don't get to know what it is).

H60.title: Tripwire
H60.text: Use the Tiny Straight reference card.

H61.title: Drone Surveilance
H61.text: Instead of assigning chips to players, assign chips to the spaces between players. Before the Showdown, each player chooses one card to add to the pocket of the chip to their left and one card to add to the pocket of the chip to their right.

H62.title: External Cameras v2
H62.text: This round, make your best 6-card hand. Use the 6-Card Hand Ranks reference card.

H63.title: Hanabi Protocol v2
H63.text: Before picking up their pocket cards, half of the players (rounded up) turn one of their cards to face away from them so that the rest of the table can see it, but they can't. Randomly determine which players have to do this.

H64.title: Antechamber Screening
H64.text: Flip all yellow chips to the dark side.

H65.title: Unlabeled Switches
H65.text: In Rounds 1-3, whenever you take a chip, flip it like a coin. If it lands on the dark side, it can no longer change hands.

H66.title: Ballad of Seat 7
H66.text: Choose a random player: deal them an extra pocket hand. This hand must be ordered in addition to the other hands.

H67.title: Owen Wilson Protocol
H67.text: Instead of distributing white chips and yellow chips, in the first 2 rounds, each player can only communicate the strength of their hand by saying "Wow" one time (with whatever inflection they want).

H68.title: Tigris and Euphrates Protocol
H68.text: In Rounds 2-4, reveal two separate sets of community cards. Once all community cards have been revealed, discard the weaker set of community cards (based on the best 5-card hand contained in it).

H69.title: Yellow and Yangtze Protocol
H69.text: In Rounds 2-4, reveal two separate sets of community cards. Each player must make the best hand they can using one of the two sets, but not both.

H70.title: Pressure Plates v2
H70.text: This round, the card(s) in High Card, Pair, Two Pair, Three of a Kind, and Full House hands that would normally determine the order of hands within those ranks are ignored for purpose of ordering hands within those ranks.

H71.title: Land Mines
H71.text: In rounds 2-4, after dealing the normal community cards, all players close their eyes while one player draws a card and holds it as high as they can reach above the table, thin-edge down, then drops it. If the card lands face-up, it becomes an additional community card.

H72.title: Footprint Scanner
H72.text: When revealing hands, reveal from best to worst. Before revealing the worst hand, all other players must guess a card value. If that value isn't in the worst pocket, you lose the heist.

H73.title: Infrared Cameras v3
H73.text: Before the Showdown, vote on one of the community cards to remove from play by simultaneously pointing at it. Lowest red chip breaks ties. Hand order must be correct before AND after removing the card. If it's impossible to remove ANY card, all players must point straight up (but the heist fails on an incorrect up-vote).

H74.title: Trackers v3
H74.text: After assigning red chips, choose a random player as the "Lab Rat." All other players reveal their hands. Reveal a card from the deck. All other players decide together whether they think that new card added as a community card would make the Lab Rat's red chip higher, lower, or the same, considering all hands. If incorrect, you lose the heist.

H75.title: Maze v2
H75.text: Reveal 4 cards from the deck. This hand, if there are exactly 1/2/3/4 Aces in play, all Aces are copies of the 1st/2nd/3rd/4th revealed card.

H76.title: Scales
H76.text: Before the Showdown, reveal cards from the deck until there are as many community + revealed cards as cards in players' pockets. All players must simultaneously vote on whether they think their pocket cards are collectively stronger, weaker, or the same as the community + revealed cards, with ties broken by the highest red chip. If incorrect, you lose the heist.

H77.title: Ghosts
H77.text:
Subtract your lowest pocket card from your highest to get the value of your ghost card, which is also in your pocket. It has no suit. 0s can be used in a 0 A 2 3 4 Straight.
A = 1, J = 11, Q = 12, K = 13

H78.title: Uniform Sequencing
H78.text: In rounds 2-4, flip two community cards (instead of 3, 1, 1).

H79.title: Reverse Time
H79.text: Round 2: Flip 1 community card Round 3: Flip 1 community card Round 4: Flip 3 community cards

H80.title: Blackjack Splits v2
H80.text: Pocket pairs are split into two hands, each of which draws an additional card (and might split again). Each time a pair comes up in the community cards, move the second card of the pair next to the first to create a parallel branch of community cards, then continue adding cards until all branches have the normal number of cards for the round (counting cards before the split as part of both branches). You must use whichever branch of the community cards creates the best hand for you.

H81.title: Stumbling Blocks
H81.text: In rounds 2 and 3, no player can take the same token as they took in the previous round.

H82.title: Two Pairs
H82.text: 2s count as two 2s (of the same suit).

H83.title: Opposite Day
H83.text: Make your best hand as normal. If half of all hands (rounded up) have the same rank, the order of all hands must be determined in reverse.

H84.title: No Turning Back
H84.text: In rounds 1-3, you cannot take a chip that is the same as or lower than any chip you've previously had that round. If it becomes impossible for anyone to take the 1-star chip, you lose the heist.

H85.title: Capitalism
H85.text: Before the Showdown, in a random order, each player must take one of the community cards into their hand, until there are none left. If there are fewer players than community cards, randomize a new order once all players have taken a card.

H86.title: Closeted Straights
H86.text: Straights can be made with repeated values (e.g. [4, 5, 5, 6, 6] is a Straight).

H87.title: Goth Queens
H87.text: If a black Queen is in play, Queens are the highest-valued cards, and Kings/Jacks are the lowest valued cards, with K > J. Straights are unaffected.

H88.title: Clones
H88.text: For each player, face cards become a copy of the highest in-play face card of their suit in the community cards and that player's hand. (If a face card is the highest of its suit, it is unchanged)

H89.title: Spider Town
H89.text: At the start of rounds 1-3, distribute all but one chip randomly among the players. You can only swap chips with your neighbors, take a chip from your neighbor, or take the one remaining chip, and cannot signal in any way for other players to swap chips. The round ends once the remaining chip is taken.

H90.title: Uppies
H90.text: For you, community cards of value 2-5 are worth the value of your highest pocket card from 6-10, if you have one.

H91.title: Sunken Cost
H91.text: After adding community cards in round 4, all players without any pocket card that could be part of a pair, Straight, or Flush raise their hands (regardless of whether that would be their best hand). Add additional community cards 2 at a time until all players have put their hands down.

H92.title: Parity Synesthesia
H92.text: Odd and Even are suits (Ace is odd, face cards are neither). A, 3, 5, 7, 9; and 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 are Straight Flushes.

H93.title: Shape Blindness
H93.text: Red and Black are suits. Flushes of Red and Black require 6 cards. For each player who could make any flush, regardless of whether it is their best hand, flush moves down 1 rank.

H94.title: Blackjack v2
H94.text: If adding the lowest card value of the flop (round 2) to your hand would make it go over 21, discard a random pocket card and draw a new one. After players have done that, if any card in the flop could be added to your hand to make it equal 21 exactly, draw another pocket card. A = 11, face cards = 10.

H95.title: Comeback
H95.text: In rounds 1-3, after chips are distributed, the player with the 1 chip draws another pocket card.

H96.title: Wealth Gap
H96.text: After chips are distributed in round 1, the player with the highest chip discards their lowest card and draws a replacement, and the player with the 1 chip discards their highest card and draws a replacement.

H97.title: Hunger Games
H97.text: Make your best hand as normal. Hands that don't involve repeated card values (Straight, Flush, etc.) must be ranked lower than hands that include repeated card values, unless you have a pocket card that is involved in a pair (whether or not the pair is part of your best hand).

H98.title: Big Club Do Trick
H98.text: Players with an unpaired pocket Club that isn't part of a Straight or Flush (regardless of whether that's your best hand) beat all players who don't have such a card.

H99.title: Clubhouse
H99.text: Make your best hand as normal. You must rank your hand below all players with more non-kicker Clubs than you.

H100.title: Never Skip Dig Day
H100.text: Any time a spade is added to a pocket or community cards, immediately add another card.

H101.title: Pride
H101.text: Hands are considered 1 rank higher than normal for each non-kicker Spade in them, but are considered the lowest hand of that rank.

H102.title: Wrath
H102.text: When a Club is revealed, discard all Clubs of lower value and draw replacements (in pockets and community cards).

H103.title: Greed
H103.text: When a non-face Diamond is revealed, all players draw an additional pocket card.

H105.title: Your Own Worst Enemy
H105.text: After dealing pocket cards, take a number of cards equal to the number of community cards that will be used and distribute them as evenly as possible among the players. Instead of community cards being drawn randomly from the deck, each community card is randomly taken from the hand of a random player with extra card(s).
H105.credit: Arman Ommid, Andrew Nathenson, Zach Adler

H106.title: Brick Wall
H106.text: Use the Small Flush Ranks reference card.

H107.title: Last-Minute Teammate Assignment
H107.text: Determine your best hand ignoring this card. The number of players whose best hand is a Pair determines where Pair falls in the rankings. 0-1: Pair is unchanged 2-3: Pair is worse than High Card 4-5: Pair is one rank better than 2 Pair 6: Pair is one rank better than 3 of a Kind Pair is permanently assigned this new rank (for this hand and future hands).

H108.title: Laughing Gas
H108.text: Until red chips are locked, any time someone laughs, add a new detrimental card.

H109.title: Underwater Vault
H109.text: After dealing pocket cards, choose a player. They can only take a chip 7 times total throughout the entire heist.

H110.title: Monogamy
H110.text: If multiple players would form a "repeated-value" rank (Pair, Three of a Kind, Full House, etc.) involving the same community card, none of them can use that card.

R1.title: Terms and Rules Clarifications
items: If a chip is on its **dark side**, it cannot be taken from a player.
**Wildcards** can have any suit and value, and must be used to make the best hand possible unless otherwise specified.
**Kicker** cards are cards that are part of your 5-card hand, but do nothing to determine the rank of your hand (i.e., they are used only as tiebreakers).
"**Sharing**" means giving information to all players.
A card is considered **revealed** if it has been shown face-up to all players simultaneously.
Beneficial modifiers are optional and can be used at any point in the hand, unless otherwise specified.
If a modifier could affect multiple cards and gives no way to distinguish them, the player chooses which card it affects. If in the community, decide collectively.
